problems.title: AdvanceWatermark cannot advance the event watermark by one event
problems.detail: internal/domain/v24_sessions.go:80-83 writes 'WHERE ... event_watermark<?' but binds the parameter as watermark-1, so an update only lands when current < target-1. My probe: a session at watermark 0 rejected target 1 with STALE_WRITER_EPOCH and left the row at 0 (P02/P03), while the same row accepted target 2 (P04/P05). By the same predicate 2->3, 3->4 ... are all refused. The doc comment promises 'moves the event watermark forward only', and 22_CLIENT_INTERFACE_DETAILS.md line 161 makes clients read events after_sequence=event_sequence one step at a time, so refusing to record the next event is a functional defect in the delivered mapping, not a style issue.
problems.why_the_check_missed_it: tests/domain/check/main.go:163,164 only exercise 0->9 and 9->3, i.e. a big jump and a backwards jump; no +1 case exists.
problems.fix: bind watermark instead of watermark-1 (or restate the intended skip rule in the comment and in the check), and add a W0301 assertion for a +1 step plus a current+2 step.

problems.title: error identities do not separate stale / sealed / missing
problems.detail: RowsAffected!=1 is reported as one canned error per function. Observed: write-after-seal returns STALE_WRITER_EPOCH not SESSION_SEALED (P16); Seal on a nonexistent session id returns SESSION_SEALED (P18); a stale epoch and an unknown id are both STALE_WRITER_EPOCH (P13/P19); a backwards watermark is also STALE_WRITER_EPOCH (P09). Card requirement 5 asks for stale/sealed/enum/hash to be distinguishable: enum (ErrUnknownProtocol) and hash (ErrBadLogHash) are genuinely distinct (P30/P31), stale vs sealed is not. Related: nothing in this layer can ever produce STALE_REVISION although 22_CLIENT_INTERFACE_DETAILS.md line 128 requires the host to answer expected_revision mismatches with STALE_REVISION - none of the four functions accepts or compares a revision, they only increment it.
problems.impact: W03-02 handlers will have to re-derive the cause from scratch or map the wrong client error.

problems.title: cross-project reference is neither implemented nor rejected, but is claimed
problems.detail: migrations/sqlite/next_v24_sessions.sql line 33-35 comments 'one run belongs to exactly one project's session index: no cross-project reuse', and receipt.json records the negative case as 'cross-project run rejected'. The index is UNIQUE(project_id, run_id), which by construction still allows the same run_id under a different project_id. I inserted ('x1',p1,run-1) and ('x2',p2,run-1): the SQL layer accepted the second row and domain.MapClientSession returned nil (V-CROSS probe, Go probe P34). What the shipped assertion W0301-RUN-UNIQUENESS actually proves is duplicate run within one project (r1/r2 both under p1). project_id also has no foreign key or existence check - store.Open already sets _foreign_keys=1, yet client_sessions accepted rows for projects p1/p2 that do not exist in domain_objects (V-INSERT-VALID, P32 rows). Card step 4 lists 跨项目引用 as something to check; it is not checked anywhere.
problems.fix: either add FOREIGN KEY(project_id) REFERENCES domain_objects(...) style enforcement / a Go-side existence check, or correct the comment and the receipt wording to 'duplicate run inside one project rejected'.

problems.title: two assertions in the check program contain tautological operands and the census hashes are thrown away
problems.detail: main.go:204 computes t1 >= t0 && strings.HasPrefix(h1, "") && seed == seed - HasPrefix(x,"") is always true and seed==seed is always true, so W0301-ADDITIVE-CENSUS reduces to a table-count comparison. The before/after census hashes h0/h1 and hAfter are assigned then discarded (main.go:178 '_ = hAfter', main.go:206 '_ = h0'), so no hash-level before/after comparison ever happens. tableStats itself (main.go:104) formats the running total rather than the per-table count, so its hash cannot see one table losing rows while another gains the same number. W0301-ADDITIVE-ROWCOUNT (total rows equal) is a real check, so the additive guarantee is still covered - just not as strongly as the assertion name suggests.
problems.fix: compare per-table counts, assert h1 != h0 only in the direction expected, and drop the always-true operands.

problems.title: VERSION-NOT-BUMPED-ON-FAILURE is weaker than its name
problems.detail: main.go:222-233 applies the migration SQL in a transaction, then only attempts the poisoned INSERT; the schema_migrations 9021 insert is never attempted inside that failing transaction, so the 'not bumped' assertion is trivially satisfied. The real property did hold when I tested it harder - I inserted version 9021 first and then the writer_epoch=0 row in one transaction and rolled back: table gone, indexes gone, versions still exactly [1..20], every existing table's row count unchanged - but the shipped assertion does not exercise that ordering.
problems.fix: do the bump then the poison in the same transaction, as applyV24 does on the success path.

problems.title: small implementation nits
problems.detail: Seal() calls time.Now() twice so sealed_at and updated_at can differ (v24_sessions.go:111-113). applyBaseline uses INSERT OR IGNORE for the version rows (main.go:57), which would swallow a genuine version collision. main.go:171 discards the error of the seeding insert. The protocol CHECK pins the single literal 'researchos-client/2', which is correct against client.protocol.schema.json (SessionSnapshot.protocol_version is a const) but means any future protocol bump needs another migration - worth recording rather than leaving implicit.

problems.title: SessionSnapshot fields that the new index cannot serve
problems.detail: Against client.protocol.schema.json SessionSnapshot (26 required), client_sessions supplies session_id/project_id/protocol_version/revision/created_at/updated_at/goal_id/active_run_id(run_id)/writer epoch/event_sequence(watermark)/native_session_ref column - so 03 v2.4 §189 and §5 are fully covered and the extra task_id, upstream_log_id/hash and sealed_at are harmless additions. Genuinely without a home anywhere in the repository today (I grepped migrations and internal/domain for each): workspace_ref and model_config_ref appear in no schema column and no non-test Go file, and WriterLease.client_id / WriterLease.expires_at are not stored (only the epoch number), so the 'single host writer' cannot be attributed to anyone even though 22 line 132/147 and HandoffResult previous_client_id/target_client_id require that identity, and 22 line 143 needs a 90-second lease expiry to revalidate. Also unrepresented: title, core_build_id, resume_requires_explicit_user, archived_at (sealed_at is a different concept: session closure vs archive), and the transcript side (earliest_event_sequence, messages, transcript_artifact_ref, has_earlier_messages) which is the event log W03-02 owns. I corrected my own first reading on one point: checkpoint_artifact_ref does have an existing home as Run.checkpoint_artifact_id (internal/domain/durability.go:109, durability_session.go:16), so it is a reuse question, not a missing field. One hard mismatch remains: SessionSnapshot.native_session_ref is required with minLength 1 while upstream_session_id is a plain nullable column with no CHECK, and the shipped check program itself inserts rows with it NULL.

problems.severity: medium, design-comparison gap the card itself asked for
problems.title: writer_epoch duplicates the existing Run.lease_epoch machinery and sits outside its restore protection
problems.detail: Card step 1 requires comparing against the existing domain schema and reusing what is already there. The repository already has a strict-increment epoch mechanism: Run objects carry lease_epoch, runtime_observations and artifact_uses key rows by (project, run, epoch) - and artifact_uses stores principal_id alongside the epoch, exactly the identity the new table omits - while internal/domain/backup_recovery.go:232-236 installs a restore-local trigger that refuses a lease_epoch increase for kind='Run' unless a fresh post-restore observation exists. client_sessions adds a second, unlinked counter (writer_epoch) with no principal column and no link to the owning Run's lease_epoch, and it is outside that barrier because the trigger predicate is literally NEW.kind='Run'. So a session and its Run can be handed off independently with nothing checking the pair, and restoring an older backup would move writer_epoch back below epochs already issued to clients, which 22_CLIENT_INTERFACE_DETAILS.md line 110 forbids ('不能因进程重启归零'). I did not execute a real restore to demonstrate that; it is read from the guard, and note the barrier table is keyed by (project, run) so it cannot cover a session id as written. This belongs in the card's own 'real field/state/index diff against the existing schema' deliverable, which receipt.json does not present.

limitations: I verified the mapping layer as it is exported today. No handler, RPC or SessionSnapshot projection exists yet, so '唯一宿主写入' is proven only in the narrow sense (all writes require a caller-supplied transaction; nothing opens a second connection). It is not yet proven that some other code path cannot bypass domain.MapClientSession and insert into client_sessions directly with raw SQL.

Concurrency and lease behaviour are untested: I did not exercise two simultaneous writers, busy_timeout contention, lease expiry (no expires_at column exists), crash-mid-handoff, or the 90s renewal loop from 22 line 143. The single-writer claim therefore rests on the epoch column plus the future W06-02 handoff handler.

My counterexamples used Python's sqlite3 as an independent implementation and my own probe used the repo's modernc driver; both agree on every CHECK/UNIQUE/rollback outcome reported. Neither is the product's real runtime database, and .local/data/researchos.sqlite was never opened for write by me - its bytes are unchanged.

I did not run the whole ./internal/... test suite (the instruction allowed the vet + targeted reruns). I ran vet over all of internal, the store package in full, the domain test compile, and three migration-sensitive domain tests; other domain tests that depend on migration files (e.g. retrieval legacy, evolution control) were not re-executed by me.

The data-contract comparison is against 03_DATA_CONTRACTS.md v2.4 lines 5/189 and the frozen client.protocol.schema.json SessionSnapshot. If the orchestrator intends client_sessions to be only a join index with business fields in domain_objects, P9 should be reclassified as a documentation requirement, not a schema requirement - I did not find that decision recorded anywhere.

Reviewer identity is self-declared; I have no attested credential separating me from the executor beyond this file, and I ran inside the same working tree rather than a separate worktree (read-only plus throwaway .local databases, tracked tree unchanged).

summary: The binding is real and the migration is genuinely minimal and safe. I rebuilt with the locked go1.27.1, got 22/22 twice, saw NOT_IMPLEMENTED exit 3 for both unregistered selectors, and confirmed the registry carries absolute GOPATH/GOCACHE plus the owner note. I then rebuilt the databases myself with a different SQLite implementation: the 0001-0020 baseline applies in order, the new file adds one table and three indexes and touches nothing else, my protocol/epoch/revision/watermark/hash/duplicate/same-project-run counterexamples are all rejected by CHECK or UNIQUE with no dirty row left behind, a failing transaction that bumps the version first still leaves the table, the indexes and version 9021 absent, and the untouched original database keeps its byte-identical sha256, its 1..20 versions and its business rows. Old work is intact: vet clean, domain tests compile, store tests pass, three migration-sensitive old tests re-run green, all 20 pinned migration hashes unchanged, .local/data byte-identical. What stops acceptance is the mapping itself: AdvanceWatermark refuses the normal one-event step (only jumps of two or more land), so the watermark the card promises to persist cannot actually be maintained event by event, and the shipped check never tests a +1 move. Behind it, stale vs sealed vs unknown-id collapse into two canned errors with no STALE_REVISION path at all, and the 'no cross-project reuse' claim is false at both the SQL and Go layers while the archived receipts state it as a passed negative. None of that endangers existing data, and all of it is small, localised and fixable in this card's files; I recommend fixing P1 with a +1/+2 assertion, tightening P2/P3 (or their wording), and adding the +1 case to the check, then re-running test.domain. P9 (workspace_ref, WriterLease client_id/expires_at, title, model_config_ref, core_build_id, resume_requires_explicit_user, archived_at, plus the nullable native ref that the protocol requires non-null) and P10 (writer_epoch is a second epoch system next to the existing Run.lease_epoch, without the principal column that artifact_uses already carries and outside the backup-restore epoch barrier) should be recorded as W03-02/W03-03/W05 obligations now, because the card's own step 1 asked for a field/state/index diff against the existing schema and neither the receipt nor any ADR presents that comparison.
